content.title: About
content.content: Bread with oatmeal is a whole‑grain loaf that incorporates whole rolled oats into the dough. It has a soft yet slightly dense crumb, a fresh‑baked aroma, and a subtle nutty note from the oats. The product is commonly enjoyed as a hearty breakfast or snack.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Oat flakes increase the fiber content of the bread, making it more filling.
Traditional oatmeal bread recipes originated in Scandinavian countries in the 19th century.
Oats contain beta‑glucans, which help lower cholesterol levels.
Oat bread is often used in weight‑control diets because of its relatively low glycemic index.
When baked, oat flakes create a crunchy crust if sprinkled on top before baking.

items.title: Rich in dietary fiber
items.content: Whole oats and whole‑grain flour provide both soluble and insoluble fiber, supporting healthy digestion.

items.title: Contains beta‑glucans
items.content: Beta‑glucans help reduce LDL cholesterol and stabilize blood glucose levels.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: The loaf supplies thiamine, niacin, and folate, which are essential for energy metabolism.

items.title: Provides minerals
items.content: It contains iron, magnesium, and zinc, important for blood formation and immune function.

items.title: Promotes satiety
items.content: The combination of carbs and protein slows digestion, helping to control appetite.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: The bread contains wheat, so it is unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: High glycemic impact if sweetened
items.content: When sugar or honey is added to the recipe, the product can raise blood sugar levels.

items.title: Phytic acid content
items.content: Oats contain phytic acid, which may reduce the absorption of certain minerals if consumed in excess.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Oat bread can be eaten plain, topped with cottage cheese, avocado, or used for sandwiches. It pairs well with honey, jam, and works nicely as a base for croutons.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the loaf in a paper bag or bread box at room temperature for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze it in an airtight bag for up to 2 months. Thaw at room temperature before use.
